pl-l4d11c3-d1e115.summary: Gives three reasons why Christ gave his flesh and blood under another species and instituted that it be received so: that faith may have merit, being of things not seen, since faith has no merit where reason supplies proof; that the mind not recoil from what the eye sees, since we do not eat raw flesh and blood, and it is not right that Christ be devoured by teeth; and that the religion not be mocked by unbelievers.
claims: Under another species faith has merit.
It prevents horror at eating flesh and blood.

pl-l4d11c3-d1e121.summary: Quotes Augustine: nothing is more reasonable than that we take the likeness of blood, so that the truth is not lacking and pagans do not ridicule us for drinking a slain man's blood; so that there be no horror of blood, you receive the sacrament in a likeness.
claims: The likeness of blood preserves the truth while avoiding horror and ridicule.

pl-l4d11c3-d1e133.summary: Concludes that it is now clear why the Lord celebrated this sacrament under another species, and this one, and instituted that we celebrate it so.

pl-l4d11c3.summary: Gives three reasons why Christ gave his flesh and blood under another species: so that faith would have merit, believing what is not seen; so that the mind would not recoil from eating raw flesh and blood; and so that unbelievers would not mock the religion. Augustine: we take a likeness of blood so that truth is not lacking and pagans cannot ridicule us for drinking a slain man's blood.
claims: Christ gave his body under another species so faith would have merit.
It was given so that the mind would not recoil.
It was given so unbelievers would not mock.
